sections.heading: What is CAC Payback Period?
paragraphs: CAC Payback Period measures how many months it takes to recover the cost of acquiring a customer . It's a critical cash flow metric that shows how quickly your acquisition investment turns profitable.

Unlike LTV:CAC ratio which shows total value, payback period focuses on time to breakeven. A shorter payback means faster reinvestment in growth. According to Bessemer Venture Partners, the benchmark is 12 months or less for healthy SaaS companies.

bullets.label: Cash Flow Management
bullets.text: Shows how long capital is tied up before generating profit

bullets.label: Growth Sustainability
bullets.text: Shorter payback means faster reinvestment cycles

bullets.label: Runway Planning
bullets.text: Critical for startups to understand burn rate implications

bullets.label: Investor Metric
bullets.text: VCs closely monitor this alongside LTV:CAC for funding decisions

sections.heading: How to Calculate CAC Payback Period
paragraphs: For example, if your CAC is $100 , with $100/month revenue and 80% gross margin , your payback is $100 / ($100 × 0.80) = 7.5 months
sections.formula: CAC Payback = CAC / (Monthly Revenue × Gross Margin %)

sections.heading: CAC Payback Benchmarks
paragraphs: Industry benchmarks from Bessemer, OpenView, and SaaS Capital (2024-2025):
Source: Bessemer Venture Partners, OpenView Partners, SaaS Capital benchmarks

bullets.label: <6 months
bullets.text: Excellent. Very efficient acquisition, consider scaling faster

bullets.label: 6-12 months
bullets.text: Good. Healthy for most SaaS companies

bullets.label: 12-18 months
bullets.text: Acceptable for enterprise. Needs optimization for SMB

bullets.label: >18 months
bullets.text: Warning. High churn risk before payback; reduce CAC or increase ARPU

sections.note: Source: Bessemer Venture Partners, OpenView Partners, SaaS Capital benchmarks

sections.heading: Payback by Business Model
paragraphs: Enterprise deals can have longer payback due to higher ACVs and lower churn.

sections.heading: How to Reduce CAC Payback Period

bullets.label: Reduce CAC
bullets.text: Improve conversion rates, focus on organic channels, optimize ad spend

bullets.label: Increase ARPU
bullets.text: Upsell to higher tiers, add premium features, usage-based pricing

bullets.label: Improve Margins
bullets.text: Reduce hosting costs, automate support, optimize infrastructure

bullets.label: Faster Onboarding
bullets.text: Get customers to value faster to reduce early churn

sections.heading: CAC Payback vs LTV:CAC
paragraphs: Both metrics matter but measure different things:
A company with great LTV:CAC (5:1) but long payback (24 months) needs significant capital to grow. A company with shorter payback can reinvest faster.

bullets.label: CAC Payback
bullets.text: Time-focused. How quickly you recover investment
LTV:CAC: Value-focused. Total return on acquisition investment
